sections.html:
Deeds in Allen County are recorded at 237 N. Main St., Suite 132, Lima, OH 45801, in the Allen Government Center next to the courthouse. The phone is (419) 223-8517. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1243, Lima, OH 45802. The counter is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:15 p.m., and shuts from 11:00 a.m. to noon for lunch.

Plan around that midday break if you are carrying a deed in yourself. Mailed documents follow a separate rule, covered below.

The recorder is the county's permanent keeper of land records and indexes each document so a title examiner can trace who owned a parcel and when. The holdings are broader than most sellers expect:

  • Deeds and mortgages, plus a daily register of both that anyone may read during business hours.
  • Liens against property for delinquent taxes.
  • Maps, plats of town lots and other land divisions, and the recorded property lines.
  • Powers of attorney.
  • Military service discharges, recorded without a fee.

A certified copy of any record is available on request for a fee that depends on page count. The office also notes that a recorder can be sued on the official bond for failing to record a document or for damaging a record.

Mail works only under one condition: the Allen County Auditor's conveyance stamp must already be on the deed. A deed that skips the auditor goes nowhere, so visit the auditor before you buy postage.

Electronic recording takes setup first:

  • Open an escrow account with the recorder.
  • Complete the e-Recording agreement, which can be downloaded from the recorder's page and mailed to the Main Street address.
  • Be ready for a possible extra fee from the e-recording vendor on top of the county's charge.

One screen applies on every route. Under ORC 317.082, a document with a Social Security number on it is refused unless an affidavit is attached or the law excludes that document. Black out the number before you bring a deed in.

Fees for each kind of document are set by law, in section 317.32. For an ordinary instrument, the first two pages cost a $17 base fee plus a $17 housing trust fund fee. Each further page adds $4 and $4. A preservation surcharge of up to $5 may also apply, and it goes to the county general fund.

Two smaller items matter to sellers. A certified copy costs $1 plus $1 per page, and filing an instrument that notes a marginal reference costs $2 plus $2 per reference. For the exact total on your papers, use the recorder's printable fee schedule.

sections.h2: Auditor charges before the deed is recorded
sections.html:
The auditor's conveyance fee is $3.00 per thousand of the purchase price, and the transfer charge is $.50 per parcel. Write checks for these to the Allen County Auditor. A conveyance form from another Ohio county is fine as long as it has four parts.

The auditor's side also settles what a buyer inherits. In Allen County, taxes follow ownership and the auditor does not prorate them, so the split belongs on the closing statement. A parcel is billed as it stood on January 1, so request a tax split if you are dividing land.

Three desks handle most of a sale, all near each other in Lima.

The auditor's site also has a property search, a tax calculator, a property sales lookup and maps. Ask the auditor whether a county transfer tax applies to your deed. That tax depends on a commissioners' resolution under section 322.02, which caps it at 30 cents per $100.

sections.h2: How a deed moves from signing to the record
sections.html:
The path has four stops. First the deed is signed and prepared, with any Social Security number removed. Second it goes to the Allen County Auditor, who stamps the conveyance and collects the conveyance fee and the transfer charge. Third the stamped deed goes to the recorder, in person, by mail or electronically. Fourth the recorder indexes it, which puts the new owner into the chain of title.

If a mortgage is being paid off, the lender's release is recorded too, and it follows the same route. Title companies handle this routinely, and most sellers never visit the counter. If you are selling on your own, call the recorder at (419) 223-8517 before you go and confirm the hours, because the lunch closing catches people out.

sections.h2: What to bring to the counter
sections.html:
• The signed deed with the auditor's conveyance stamp on it.
  • A check for the recording fee. The page count drives the total, so ask for the fee schedule if you are unsure.
  • Any mortgage release or other document that has to be filed along with the deed.
  • The e-Recording agreement and escrow account details, if you plan to file electronically.

Ask for a certified copy once the deed is recorded if you want proof for your own files. The fee for a certified copy is $1 plus $1 per page.

Allen County had 100,881 residents in July 2025. It has 44,946 housing units, and 67.7 percent were owner-occupied in 2020 to 2024. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $165,300. Lima is the county seat and largest city.

Work in this order. Confirm who is on title, call the treasurer about any balance, get the auditor's stamp, then record. A closing agent normally handles the last two steps. If you do them yourself, bring a deed with no Social Security number on it.

If you inherited the house, ask the probate court which papers support a deed. Open repairs or a tenant in the house do not change the recording steps, although a mortgage payoff adds a release for the recorder to file. A cash sale skips the lender's payoff, but the stamp, the fees and the recording still happen the same way.

faqs.q: Does the Allen County recorder close for lunch?
faqs.a: Yes. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:15 p.m., and closed from 11:00 a.m. to noon.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the Allen County recorder?
faqs.a: Yes, but only with the Allen County Auditor's conveyance stamp already on it. Without the stamp, a mailed conveyance is refused.

faqs.q: Does Allen County accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: Yes, for filers who set up an escrow account and file a completed e-Recording agreement. The e-recording vendor may charge its own fee.

faqs.q: Are military discharge records free to record in Allen County?
faqs.a: Yes. There is no fee to record military service discharges.

faqs.q: Why was my deed refused for a Social Security number?
faqs.a: Ohio Revised Code 317.082 bars the recorder from taking a document with one unless an affidavit is attached or the law excludes the document. Black the number out of the copy you submit, or ask the closing agent how to handle it.
